draft.title: Homeostasis and negative feedback
card: Homeostasis is the way an organism keeps its internal conditions steady, even when the outside environment changes. Examples are body temperature and blood glucose.
A feedback loop has three parts. A receptor detects a change. A control centre processes the information. An effector carries out a response.
the response reverses the change that was detected. The condition moves back towards its normal range, and the response then switches off.
Most homeostatic systems use negative feedback. A condition rarely stays at one exact value. It moves up and down around a set point.
draft.remember: Negative feedback: detect a change, then respond to reverse it.

a.q: What makes a feedback loop a negative feedback loop?
opts: The response reverses the change that was detected
The response is small and slow to start
The response makes the change bigger
The response happens only when conditions are normal
a.why: In negative feedback the response works against the change and moves the condition back towards normal. The tempting option about making the change bigger describes the opposite, where the response adds to the change.
a.clue: Think about which way the response pushes compared with the change.

b.q: Sam's body is warmed by exercise and his core temperature rises above its normal range. His body responds and his temperature falls back. Why is this negative feedback?
opts: The response reverses the rise in temperature
The temperature fell, which means it was a negative change
The body stopped detecting the temperature
The response made the temperature stay higher
b.why: The change was a rise, and the response cooled the body so the temperature moved back towards normal. The word negative describes the response working against the change, not the temperature going down. A rise that the response then made bigger would not be negative feedback.
b.clue: Compare the direction of the response with the direction of the original change.

a.best: The response reverses the change that was detected

b.best: The response reverses the rise in temperature
